items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I don't know who told me that, Richard M. Jones or somebody, that they'd heard Bolden say that.

ctx.x: I think it was King Oliver who said that he wanted his band to be able to play so soft they could hear the dancers shuffling.

Yeah, I think that's quoted in Jasmine as a Bolden remark, whether it was, yeah, it was supposed to be a Bolden remark. They say, way down, way down low, so I can hear those whores drag their feet on the floor. I don't know who told me that, Richard M. Jones or somebody, that they'd heard Bolden say that. I don't know whether it's strictly true, but anyway, that was very much the New Orleans tradition. The Ori band followed that.
What was that? Was that for the, part of the form of it, the definite form, or did it build momentum towards the end, or?

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: Richard M. Jones died about 1946 in January, I believe. And I'd interviewed him a couple of times and have fairly good interviews.

ctx.x: Mrs. Rankin's supposed to keep after me.

Keep after me. But I've made notes also of the ones that I will send. I have a big sheet. I see. The Clarence Williams notes are especially in very bad shape. But I'll try to enlarge a little bit and correct what is here. And send those. Another man who's dead. Clarence Williams isn't dead, but unfortunately is in very bad health. Richard M. Jones died about 1946 in January, I believe. And I'd interviewed him a couple of times and have fairly good interviews. He was a very important figure in the Chicago scene. I…
If you want to do it.
